rubrics.justification: Generally recognizes a blastocyst with identifiable ICM and TE, but overstates confidence from a single blurred image and is somewhat inconsistent with the provided expansion grade, calling it more full than expanded.

Integrates age, ovarian reserve, semen quality, prior cycle history, unexplained infertility, and endometrial thickness well with embryo quality, though BMI 17.2 is labeled normal rather than underweight/borderline low.

Reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, with conclusions broadly supported by embryo grade and patient factors; minor issues include some overinterpretation of morphology and slight ambiguity around grading nomenclature.

Recommendations are largely consistent with IVF practice guidelines: SET for a good-quality day-5 blastocyst in a young patient, caution against unproven add-ons, and selective rather than routine PGT-A. Minor deviations include a somewhat rigid emphasis on >=8 mm lining as ideal.

Provides practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, including SET, review of endometrial preparation, luteal support, and uterine reassessment if unsuccessful; useful though not highly protocol-specific.
